problem: Model-free RL for image-based navigation needs huge amounts of environment interaction, which is prohibitively costly on real robots. Sim-to-real needs photorealistic simulators, and prior real-imagery RL navigation trained and tested on the same environment.
motivation: Real robots need navigation policies that generalise to deployment-time appearance changes without fine-tuning. A single recorded traversal can act as a cheap world model, but a finite graph invites memorisation and overfitting.
key_idea: Build a topological navigation graph from one real coverage traversal, precompute frozen CNN features, and train an A3C goal-image-conditioned agent with cheap stochastic augmentation (frame selection, feature-space noise, stochastic transitions) at over 20K transitions/s, then deploy it on a real robot without fine-tuning.
insight: Making memorisation impossible via nondeterminism in observations (about 30 extra frames per node, small rotations, feature-space Ornstein-Uhlenbeck and local noise via a Taylor/Jacobian approximation) and transitions (stutter) lets a policy trained on a fixed recording transfer to weeks-later real conditions. ImageNet and Places365 encoders give comparable learning curves, while an untrained encoder does worse (Fig. 4a). Failures come from perceptual shift (sun glare, shadows, rain, people): the localisation readout is less crisp at deployment, and the failed trajectory 6 was on a rarely used route with large lighting change.
method: Navigation graph: 2099 nodes spaced 1 m (over 2 km, campus plus 7 floors of 2 buildings) from a single teleoperated traversal with omnidirectional camera; loop closures and duplicate regions annotated by hand; rotation simulated by cropping the panorama.
Action space: turn left/right by 90°, move forward 1 m, and 7 elevator actions (one per destination floor), 10 discrete actions in total.
Nondeterministic frame selection: observations sampled from images within 0.5 m of the node plus rotation up to 8°, giving over 250,000 real observations (about 120 per node).

Feature-space noise: temporally correlated OU brightness noise pushed through the encoder with a first-order Jacobian approximation, plus uncorrelated Gaussian noise scaled by the Jacobian, applied to precomputed embeddings.
Stochastic transitions: each forward move leaves the agent in place with probability 0.05.

Agent: frozen pretrained ResNet18 (Places365) with strided mean pooling to a 4096-d embedding for observation and goal image, then FC-256, an LSTM-256 with previous action, and softmax policy plus value head; trained with A3C (128 workers).
Curriculum: 100 levels by optimal path length (5 m up to 403 m), advancing when success reaches 80%; sparse reward of 1 at the goal.

setting.backbone: Frozen pretrained ResNet18 (Places365) encoder + FC/LSTM policy trained with A3C from scratch
setting.training_data: A single real coverage traversal (2099 nodes, ~250K augmented observations) on a Pioneer 3DX campus, plus pretrained encoder weights (Places365/ImageNet); ~1B environment timesteps of RL in the replay environment
setting.observation: Omnidirectional monocular RGB images (observation and goal image), 224x896 panoramic crops
setting.action_space: Discrete high-level: turn left/right 90°, forward 1 m, 7 elevator floor actions
setting.simulator: Custom interactive replay of real recorded data (topological graph); real robot for deployment
setting.privileged: Goal given as an image; human-annotated loop closures for the graph at training time; human operator executes high-level actions and a laser rangefinder is used for obstacle avoidance at deployment; no GT map at test time

numbers.bench: other:Campus real-robot goal-image navigation (2 km, 11 starts)
numbers.eval_set_note: 11 real-robot trials to one fixed goal, 3 weeks after training data
numbers.extra: Success = within 2 m of goal image location; human executes actions; laser obstacle avoidance; no fine-tuning
numbers.evidence: Agent navigated successfully ... in ten of the eleven trials; Tab. 1 avg ratio 2.42; 1.14 times farther for the virtual agent

numbers_note: Only a small real-robot evaluation; no standard benchmark. Training-data path ratio ~1.35 average over 100K episodes (Fig. 5).
results: The agent reached the goal in 10 of 11 real-robot trials, three weeks after data collection, without fine-tuning. Deployed paths averaged 2.42x the optimal length versus 1.14x for the virtual agent on the same paths (about 1.35x over 100K random training episodes). Trajectory 6 failed after over 1 km; there is no learned baseline comparison.
limitations: Small real-world evaluation (11 trials, one goal) with no baselines; high-level actions were executed by a human operator, and the laser provides safety.
Deployment paths are much longer (2.42x optimal) due to perceptual gaps such as sun glare, shadows, rain and people; one failure.
Requires a coverage traversal and manual loop-closure annotation, and the policy is tied to that specific environment/graph.
